chunks: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, who said:

Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام was asked about a man who has contact with a woman in a manner short of the private part: is ghusl upon her if he ejaculates while she does not ejaculate? He said: "There is no ghusl upon her; and if he does not ejaculate, then there is no ghusl upon him."

key_terms.الرَّجُلِ: the man involved in the ruling
key_terms.الْفَرْجِ: the private part; here, indicating full sexual intercourse
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةَ: the woman involved in the ruling
key_terms.عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: peace be upon him; honorific for the Imam
key_terms.غُسْلٌ: ritual bath required in certain states of major ritual impurity

ai.seo_question: When is ghusl required after intimate contact that does not involve intercourse?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding ghusl in a case of sexual contact short of vaginal intercourse. It states that ghusl is not required of the woman if only the man ejaculates, and that ghusl is not required of the man if he does not ejaculate.
